name: Progressive Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis Type 2

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the ABCB11 gene
Chronic intrahepatic cholestasis presenting in infancy or early childhood
Elevated serum bile acids with normal or mildly elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)
Liver biopsy showing canalicular cholestasis with absence or marked reduction of BSEP protein expression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical cholestasis with elevated serum bile acids and genetic confirmation of ABCB11 mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy and immunohistochemistry may support diagnosis but are not mandatory if genetic testing is conclusive.

pathognomonic.notes: Intense itching often leading to excoriations

searchTerms: progressive yellowing of skin from bile buildup

pathognomonic.symptomName: Low or normal serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) despite cholestasis
searchTerms: low or normal GGT despite bile flow problems
fatty stools from poor fat absorption

common.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
common.notes: May cause coagulopathy and bone disease
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K

occasional.symptomName: Jaundice exacerbations during infections or fasting
searchTerms: jaundice worsens with infection or fasting
bilirubin spikes after fasting or infection

occasional.symptomName: Mild developmental delay secondary to chronic illness
searchTerms: slow development due to chronic sickness

rare.notes: Increased risk especially in untreated or advanced disease

imaging: Ultrasound may show hepatomegaly and exclude biliary obstruction
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in ABCB11 gene encoding Bile Salt Export Pump (BSEP)
other: Liver biopsy showing canalicular cholestasis and absent or reduced BSEP protein by immunostaining

distinguishingFeatures: Low GGT cholestasis but with different clinical course
Abnormal bile acid profiles on specialized testing
May respond to bile acid replacement therapy
Different genetic mutations affecting bile acid synthesis enzymes

redFlags: Onset of severe pruritus and jaundice in infancy
Persistently low or normal GGT despite cholestasis
Development of hepatocellular carcinoma in a young child
references: Strautnieks SS, et al. 'A gene encoding a liver-specific ABC transporter is mutated in progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis.' Nat Genet. 1998.
Bull LN, et al. 'A gene encoding a P-type ATPase mutated in two forms of hereditary cholestasis.' Nat Genet. 1998.
European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) Clinical Practice Guidelines on cholestatic liver diseases. J Hepatol. 2017.
